about.title: Ontario Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Eighteen people died on Ontario's roads in 2025, according to public collision records for that year. Each of those numbers was somebody's parent, partner, or child, and the paperwork that follows a death rarely waits for grief to settle. We're here to take one task off your plate. Our team handles wrongful death claims in San Bernardino County. Fatal crashes here tend to occur along the region's heaviest commuter and freight routes: I-10 through the center of the city, Euclid Avenue, SR-60 to the south, and I-15 along the east side. Wrongful death is not only about traffic, though. A fall on a neglected property, a defective product, or a preventable medical error can support a claim as well. Under California law, a spouse, domestic partner, or child typically has the first right to file, and the clock generally runs two years from the date of death. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless your family recovers something.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, with the spouse or domestic partner and children first in line and certain dependents or heirs after that. We can sort out who in your family has the right to bring the claim.

items.title: The deadline is real, and sometimes shorter
items.desc: Most California wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but that window shrinks considerably when a government entity is involved. Getting our team in place early protects that timeline.

items.title: A claim that reflects the whole loss
items.desc: Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to include the financial support the person would have provided and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We will build the claim around what your family actually lost.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on the I-10 in Ontario and the other driver is facing charges. Do we have to wait for the criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs separately from any criminal prosecution the San Bernardino County District Attorney may pursue. The two cases can move at the same time, and the outcome of one does not decide the other. Waiting for the criminal case to finish could put your two-year filing deadline at risk, so it is worth speaking with us sooner rather than later.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California gives the first right to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If there are none, certain other dependents and heirs may qualify, and the rules can get detailed depending on family structure. We can review your situation and explain who has standing before anything is filed.

items.question: What if a city vehicle or a public agency was involved in the death?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity in California follow a much shorter timeline than the standard two years, and they usually require filing a formal claim with the agency before a lawsuit can begin. Missing that step can end the case before it starts. If there is any chance a public agency, road contractor, or government employee played a role, mention it right away so we can act within the shorter deadline.
